newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-MATURANA'S ECUADOR FACE CRUCIAL GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATURANA'S ECUADOR FACE CRUCIAL GAME.

text.p: Ecuador, with altitude on their side and an inferiority complex hopefully in their past, meet Chile on Sunday in a match which is crucial to their bid to reach the World Cup for the first time.

Coached by Francisco Maturana, the man who led his native Colombia out of the soccer wilderness, Ecuador need a win to keep themselves in the hunt for one of the four World Cup places allocated to South America.
The Ecuadoreans need to win their home games as they are notoriously poor travellers.
Chile, despite lying eighth, are only one point below fourth-placed Bolivia and play their last four games at home, where they have not yet dropped a point.
Ecuador, who have no real tradition at international level, have already caused major shocks in Quito, at 2,800 metres above sea level, by beating Uruguay 4-0 and Argentina 2-0.

Maturana claims the secret is the team's new-found confidence. "A short time ago, we overcame our fear. I now see a team that always wishes the game was tomorrow," said the man who led his own country to two successive World Cups.
Chile inflicted Ecuador's worst defeat in the qualifiers when they won 4-1 in Santiago last year but Maturana said: "Anyone who saw that game knows the score is a lie."
Paraguay, who do not play on Sunday, lead the group with 23 points from 10 games and, enjoying a six-point advantage over second-placed Colombia, appear to have one place sewn up.
The remaining three are up for grabs as the single nine-team group provides a fascinating battle.

Third-placed Argentina have 16 points and are followed by Bolivia, Ecuador, Uruguay and Peru with 13. Chile have 12 points and only Venezuela, with a measly one point from 10 games, are out of the race.
Colombia at one stage appeared to be easy qualifiers but have faltered badly, losing their three games and scoring only one goal in the process.
On Sunday they are away to Uruguay, the two times world champions who no longer inspire the fear they used to among their South American rivals.

"This will be a do-or-die match," said Colombia coach Hernan Dario Gomez, whose team will be without suspended strikers Faustino Asprilla and Victor Aristizabal. Colombia need at least a point to avoid being dragged into the pack below them.
Argentina, hugely criticised for performances which have included defeats by Ecuador and Bolivia, are at home to Peru, who are buoyant after a shock win in Colombia in their last game.
Coach Daniel Passarella has once again left Fiorentina's Gabriel Batistuta out of the squad, claiming he and striker Hernan Crespo are incompatible.
Bolivia, whose chances are reduced because they only have one game left, will expect to pick up maximum points away to a disintegrating Venezuelan team.

Venezuela striker Diony Guerra has been barred for indiscipline while second-choice goalkeeper Gilberto Angelucci pulled out because he did not want to leave his Argentine club San Lorenzo if he were not guaranteed a game.
